identity.name: CRYOGENIC OGS LIMITED
identity.industry: Oil & Gas Terminal Automation & Critical Flow Measurement

summary.oneLiner: Cryogenic OGS is pivoting from a low-value fabricator to a high-margin system integrator by capturing full scope revenue on metering skids and launching indigenous density probes to replace imports. Strong H1FY26 growth (57% YoY) is driven by large export orders (Egypt/Nigeria) and deepening PSU relationships, with capacity headroom to double revenue before major capex.

one-line thesis: Cryogenic OGS is pivoting from a low-value fabricator to a high-margin system integrator by capturing full scope revenue on metering skids and launching indigenous density probes to replace imports. Strong H1FY26 growth (57% YoY) is driven by large export orders (Egypt/Nigeria) and deepening PSU relationships, with capacity headroom to double revenue before major capex.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +57% YoY (H1FY26); EBITDA Margin: ~30% (expanded via turnkey model); PAT: Significant rise (specific number not disclosed, impacted by 1.24 Cr one-off capital gain tax); Order Book: 22-25 Cr confirmed + 65 Cr bids submitted; Net Debt: Zero. One-offs: 1.24 Cr exceptional item related to capital gain tax on factory sale in H1FY26.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Expect similar H2FY26 growth as H1 (implied ~50%+ full year); Margin: Aim to maintain ~30% EBITDA, potential upside from international mix; Order Inflow: Aggressive pursuit of LNG and international projects; Capex: New facility planning initiated, expected need in 2-3 years at 75-100 Cr revenue threshold.
order book & pipeline: 22-25 Crores (confirmed post-sales); 65 Crores (bids submitted); Key projects include 143 truck loading skids for Egypt (Emerson) and custody transfer skid for Honeywell Nigeria.
segment / subsidiary detail: Core: Metering skids (custody transfer), Air eliminators, Basket strainers (80-90% market share in catalog items for PSUs). New: aDENS Density Probe (import substitute, 3-4 initial orders). Diversification: Nacelle lifting jigs for Suzlon (Wind energy).
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Transition to full turnkey model (procuring high-value valves/meters) increasing ticket size and value add. 2) aDENS density probe replacing European imports in tank farms. 3) International expansion (Middle East/Africa) with better margins. 4) LNG and Green Hydrogen metering technologies.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margins ~30% sustained despite higher pass-through costs in turnkey model due to: 1) Better procurement pricing vs MNCs. 2) Value capture in design/engineering selection. 3) Higher margin profile of international projects vs domestic.
capex / expansion: Current utilization 35-40%. Existing 8,300 sqm facility can support doubling of revenue. Significant capex for new facility planned in 2-3 years when revenue hits 75-100 Cr range.
capital allocation: Zero-debt balance sheet. IPO proceeds and operating cash (27 Cr cash on hand) allocated to working capital for turnkey procurement (valves/meters) and gradual new facility development.
risks & watch-items: 1) Customer Concentration: Top 10 customers = 89% of revenue (dependent on EPC spend by IOCL/BPCL). 2) Execution Risk: Scaling turnkey model requires working capital management. 3) Raw Material/Component dependency on imports for high-end instruments.
management quality / tone: Confident and aggressive on growth; emphasizing 'financial discipline' and 'zero debt' while pivoting business model. Transparent about capacity constraints and future capex needs.
non-obvious takeaways: The company holds an 80-90% market share in specific catalog items (air eliminators/strainers) across 200+ PSU terminals, creating a massive installed base for 10-year replacement cycles. The 'aDENS' probe approval is in Cryogenic's name, legally blocking the European tech partner from direct entry into India.

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.
